mutants.label: retrain-daily-instead-of-monthly
mutants.find: result = walk_forward(pairs, model, start, end, retrain="monthly")
mutants.replace: result = walk_forward(pairs, model, start, end, retrain="daily")

mutants.label: pairs-read-without-the-end-date-bound
mutants.why: Rows with run_date after `end` can reach neither a prediction (walk_forward evaluates run dates in [start, end] only) nor a training set (their windows close after any issuance in range, and fit/update take window_end_utc < T). So the predicate is a read-size optimisation for the 6M-row table, and dropping it changes no output row; the comment above the query says exactly that. Inert on values, only memory differs; the unit test seeds rows after the end date to keep it that way.

mutants.label: station-features-keyed-by-the-cli-station
mutants.why: In the registry seed (dbt/seeds/station_registry.csv, 573 rows) cli_station equals icao on every row -- checked by loading it -- so the two keys select identical strings and the resulting station table is identical. Inert on the shipped registry; it would matter only for a future registry row where the CLI identifier differs from the ICAO code, which is a seed-data change rather than a code defect.

mutants.label: pair-columns-without-cycle-hour
mutants.why: cycle_hour is a model feature whose value is constant in the synthetic and fixture data (13 / one regime), and the booster routes a missing column as NaN for every row; with one distinct value the feature has no split to make, so predictions are identical with or without it. The unit-level matrix oracle (test_challenger.py) pins that the model consumes it when present; this CLI test cannot see a column whose value never varies. Real archives carry 00/06/12/18 and would differ.

mutants.label: init-db-not-run-before-the-read
mutants.why: init_db is `create ... if not exists`, and the loader's insert needs raw.model_predictions, so on a database that has never been initialised the mutant fails in load_predictions rather than silently; on any database the pipeline has touched (every fixture here ingests or runs init-db first) the two are identical. Not a silent-wrong-output mutant: the failure, where it exists, is a loud catalog error one statement later.
